title: CLEAR Destination Guide: NYC on a Layover
summary: Planning an NYC layover? Learn when to leave JFK, LaGuardia, or Newark, how to reach the city, and what you can do before your next flight.
body_markdown:
A long layover in New York City does not have to mean waiting at the airport. With enough time, you can explore a neighborhood, visit a landmark, or have a great meal before your next flight.


This guide covers John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), LaGuardia Airport (LGA), and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), including how long it takes to reach the city and what you can realistically do during your connection.
‍


## **Should You Leave the Airport During an NYC Layover?**


Before making plans, work backward from your next flight’s boarding time. Include the trip into the city, possible traffic or transit delays, the return to the airport, and enough time for airport security.


Terminal changes and checked bags can also take time. If you need to collect and recheck luggage, change terminals, or clear customs, a city trip may not be practical even with a longer layover.
‍


## **What Should You Do with Your Luggage?**


Confirm whether your checked bags will transfer to your next flight or need to be collected and rechecked. If you are bringing bags into the city, let your luggage shape your plans.


A taxi or rideshare may be easier with several bags. Subway and train trips can involve stairs, transfers, and walking. If you have heavy bags and cannot store them, staying at the airport may be the better choice.


At JFK, Smarte Carte offers[baggage storage](https://smartecarte.com/john-f-kennedy/#baggageStorage) in Terminals 1 and 4. Hours vary, so confirm availability and include drop-off and pickup time in your itinerary.


LaGuardia and Newark do not offer luggage storage services. Both airports offer baggage carts and other luggage assistance, but those services do not provide a place to leave bags during a city visit. Plan to keep your bags with you or arrange off-airport storage in advance, allowing enough time for drop-off and pickup.
‍


## **JFK Layovers**


### **Getting Into Manhattan From JFK**


Take the AirTrain to Jamaica Station, where you can connect to the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR) for Grand Central Madison or Penn Station. You can also take the AirTrain to Howard Beach and connect to the A subway line.


The LIRR is usually the more direct option for the Midtown itineraries in this guide. According to[JFK’s AirTrain guide](https://www.jfkairport.com/transportation/airtrain) , the AirTrain costs $8.75 when entering or exiting at Jamaica or Howard Beach. Travel between airport terminals is free.


Allow about 45 to 60 minutes to reach Manhattan via the AirTrain and LIRR, including the transfer. Check current schedules before leaving the airport.


Changing terminals? JFK’s terminals are not connected after airport security. Take the AirTrain to your next terminal and leave enough time to clear airport security again.


### **Less Than 6 Hours: Stay at JFK**


With less than 6 hours, staying at JFK is usually more practical, especially if you need to change terminals or recheck bags. Use our[JFK Airport Guide](https://www.clearme.com/blog/airport-guide-jfk) to find restaurants, shopping, and other ways to spend your layover.


### **6 to 8 Hours: Explore Midtown**


Take the LIRR to Grand Central Madison. Stop for a New York slice at[Uncle Paul’s Pizza](https://unclepaulspizzamenu.com/) on Vanderbilt Avenue, then walk to Bryant Park and the New York Public Library.


If time allows, continue up Fifth Avenue toward[Rockefeller Center](https://www.rockefellercenter.com/explore) . Keep your plans close to Midtown so the return to Grand Central remains straightforward.


### **8 Hours or More: Choose One NYC Experience**


With 8 hours or more, choose one area rather than trying to cross the city several times.
‍


#### **Central Park and Fifth Avenue**


Walk north from Grand Central Madison toward Rockefeller Center and Fifth Avenue before continuing to the southern end of[Central Park](https://www.centralparknyc.org/activities/guides/explore-the-south-end) . Explore the park or visit[The Museum of Modern Art](https://www.moma.org/) nearby.
‍


#### **Lower Manhattan**


Visit the[9/11 Memorial](https://www.911memorial.org/visit/memorial) and[One World Observatory](https://www.oneworldobservatory.com/) , then walk through the Financial District toward Wall Street and The Battery. Check hours and ticket availability before your trip.
‍


#### **DUMBO and the Brooklyn Bridge**


Head to[Brooklyn Bridge Park](https://brooklynbridgepark.org/) for waterfront views. Explore[DUMBO](https://dumbo.nyc/) and stop for coal-fired pizza at[Juliana’s Pizza](https://www.julianaspizza.com/brooklyn) on Old Fulton Street. If time allows, walk across the[Brooklyn Bridge](https://brooklynbridgepark.org/places-to-see/brooklyn-bridge/) toward Manhattan.
‍


#### **Chinatown and the Lower East Side**


Start in Chinatown with a roast pork bun at[Mei Lai Wah](https://meilaiwahnyc.com/) on Mott Street, a Hong Kong-style bakery with deep roots in the neighborhood. From there, visit[Nom Wah Tea Parlor](https://www.nomwah.com/chinatown/) , which first opened in 1920, for a dim sum feast. If you have time—and room for another bite—walk toward the Lower East Side and stop at the original[Russ & Daughters](https://www.russanddaughters.com/) on East Houston Street, a New York institution known for Jewish specialties like bagels and smoked fish.


‍


## **LaGuardia Layovers**


### **Getting Around From LaGuardia**


LaGuardia is the closest major airport to Midtown Manhattan, and offers especially easy access to Queens neighborhoods such as Jackson Heights and Astoria.


LaGuardia does not have direct rail service. The free[Q70 LaGuardia Link](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/transportation/public-transport) connects Terminals B and C with subway and LIRR service in Jackson Heights. The bus ride is about 10 minutes, though traffic can affect the trip.


Allow for about 30 to 60 minutes to reach Midtown, depending on traffic and your transportation choice. With several bags, a taxi or rideshare may be more practical than transferring to the subway.


If your connection requires a terminal change, leave extra time. Use LaGuardia’s complimentary[All Terminals Shuttle](https://www.laguardiaairport.com/transportation/all-terminals-shuttle) and plan to clear airport security again.


### **Less Than 5 Hours: Stay at LaGuardia**


With less than 5 hours, staying at LaGuardia is usually more practical, especially if you need to change terminals or recheck bags. Check out our[LaGuardia Airport Guide](https://www.clearme.com/blog/airport-guide-lga) to find New York restaurants, shopping, public art, and other things to do.


### **5 to 7 Hours: Explore Queens**


For a shorter trip outside the airport, choose a neighborhood nearby in Queens to wander around.
‍


#### **Jackson Heights for Food**


Take the[Q70](https://bustime.mta.info/?search=Q70-SBS) to Jackson Heights. Stop for momos at[Nepali Momo Cafe](https://nepalimomocafe.com/) or try Colombian food at[Arepa Lady](https://www.thearepalady.com/) before exploring 37th Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue.
‍


#### **Astoria for Greek Food and the Park**


Head to Astoria for Greek specialties at[Taverna Kyclades](https://www.tavernakyclades.com/) , then continue to[Astoria Park](https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/astoria-park) for views across the East River.


### **8 Hours or More: Choose Queens, Brooklyn or Manhattan**


With 8 hours or more, Brooklyn and Manhattan become more realistic. Choose one area and keep your itinerary focused.
‍


#### **Tour Citi Field**


Baseball fans can take a[tour of Citi Field](https://www.mlb.com/mets/ballpark/hospitality/tours) , home of the New York Mets. Public tours take about 60 minutes and may include the warning track, press conference room, suites, and ballpark clubs. Tour dates and access vary, so check availability in advance.


Traveling with bags? Review[Citi Field’s bag policy](https://www.mlb.com/mets/ballpark/information/bag-policy) before booking. Backpacks are generally prohibited, and other permitted bags cannot exceed 16 by 16 by 8 inches.
‍


#### **Williamsburg and Greenpoint**


Head to Williamsburg for a slice at[L’Industrie Pizzeria](https://www.lindustriebk.com/) , then explore the neighborhood’s shops and East River waterfront. Continue into Greenpoint for pierogi at[Pierozek](https://www.pierozekbrooklyn.com/) on Manhattan Avenue.
‍


#### **Central Park and the Upper East Side**


If Manhattan is your priority, head toward the Upper East Side and the eastern side of[Central Park](https://www.centralparknyc.org/) . Spend time in the park, walk along Fifth Avenue, or choose one nearby museum.
‍


## **Newark Layovers**


### **Getting Into Manhattan From Newark Airport**


Take[AirTrain Newark](https://www.newarkairport.com/transportation/airtrain) to[Newark Liberty International Airport Station](https://www.njtransit.com/station/newark-airport-rail-station) , then connect to NJ Transit to New York Penn Station. According to[NJ Transit](https://www.njtransit.com/destinations/newark-liberty-international-airport) , the train to Midtown takes about 30 minutes and costs $17.25 one way for an adult, including the AirTrain fare.


Allow extra time to reach the airport station from your terminal.[AirTrain Newark](https://www.newarkairport.com/transportation/airtrain) connects terminals ,if you need to transfer to a different terminal, you may need to clear airport security again.


### **Less Than 6 Hours: Stay at Newark**


With less than 6 hours, staying at EWR is the practical decision, especially if you need to change terminals or recheck bags. Take a look at our[Newark Liberty International Airport Guide](https://www.clearme.com/blog/airport-guide-ewr) to find restaurants, shopping, public art, and other things to do.


### **6 to 8 Hours: Choose Newark or Midtown**


With 6 to 8 hours, choose one area and keep your plans focused.
‍


#### **The Ironbound and Downtown Newark**


Take the train to Newark Penn Station and explore the Ironbound. Walk along Ferry Street and stop for Brazilian rodizio at[Casa Nova Grill](https://www.casanova-grill.com/) or a casual Brazilian meal at[Altas Horas Lanches](https://www.facebook.com/altashoraslanches/) .


From there, head toward[Independence Park](https://essexcountyparks.org/parks/independence-park) or[Riverfront Park](https://essexcountyparks.org/parks/riverfront-park) . For a taste of Newark history, visit[Hobby’s Delicatessen](https://www.hobbysdeli.com/) , a family-run Jewish deli whose roots in the city stretch back more than a century.
‍


#### **Koreatown and the Empire State Building**


Take NJ Transit to[New York Penn Station](https://www.njtransit.com/station/new-york-penn-station) , then walk east for a meal in Koreatown and a visit to the Empire State Building. Keeping your plans nearby makes the return to Penn Station easier.
‍


#### **Tour Madison Square Garden**


[Madison Square Garden](https://www.msg.com/) is directly above Penn Station, making it an easy stop from Newark Airport. The[guided tour](https://www.msg.com/guided-tours/new-york-city-tours/madison-square-garden-tour) takes about 60 minutes and may include backstage areas, luxury suites, and views inside the arena. Check tour availability before your trip.


Traveling with bags? Review[Madison Square Garden’s bag policy](https://www.msg.com/madison-square-garden/faqs) before booking. Bags must fit comfortably under your seat, and bags larger than 22 by 14 by 9 inches are prohibited. Policies can vary by event, so check the details for your visit before you go.
‍


#### **Pizza and the High Line**


From Penn Station, grab a slice at[NY Pizza Suprema](https://www.nypizzasuprema.com/) then head toward Hudson Yards. Walk a section of the[High Line](https://www.thehighline.org/) before returning to Penn Station.


### **8 Hours or More: Explore Lower Manhattan**


With eight hours or more, Lower Manhattan becomes more realistic. Visit the[9/11 Memorial](https://www.911memorial.org/visit/memorial) and[One World Observatory](https://www.oneworldobservatory.com/) , then walk through the Financial District toward Wall Street and Battery Park.
‍


## **How Early Should You Return to the Airport?**


As a general rule, plan to return at least two hours before a domestic flight and three hours before an international flight. Give yourself more time during busy travel periods, when checking bags, traffic, or transit delays could affect your return.


Work backward from your boarding time, not only your scheduled departure. Before leaving the city, check your flight, transit conditions, and current airport security wait times.

At[JFK](https://www.clearme.com/all-locations/john-f-kennedy-international-airport) , the CLEAR+ Lanes are available in Terminal 4, and at[LGA](https://www.clearme.com/all-locations/laguardia-airport) , CLEAR+ eGates are in Terminal C.
